title: Rack and roadmap — field notes
content:
2026-03-09 21:45 — quick log while still in rack A

Context: Solo night run for customer ACME-Edge (small regional dc). Primary goal: validate rack wiring, confirm GPU nodes boot with our appliance image, and capture environment quirks for handoff. Not for public; scratch notes.

High-level summary (what matters)
- Power feeds: PDU1 -> A&B, PDU2 -> C&D (labels swapped in room, see below).
- Network: Leaf-1 is on VLAN 210 (management). Customer uses overlapping RFC1918 with our default test ranges; must avoid 10.0.0.0/16.
- KMS: Customer HSM available but requires key-wrap policy change (blocked).
- Appliances: 3 nodes in rack (n1-n3) booted; n2 threw firmware nvram warning — will schedule BIOS update.

Checklist (done / in-progress)
- [x] Rack power map photo (phone) uploaded to ticket JIRA-PRIV-1245. Filename: acme-rackA-power-20260309.jpg
- [x] Verify PDU load: left PDU measured ~6.2A under idle, right PDU ~5.8A.
- [x] Rack U positions annotated on sticker (U1-U46).
- [x] Appliance image v2.3.1 deployed to USB, PXE disabled per customer request.
- [x] Nodes n1,n2,n3: installed OS image, joined local mgmt switch, started redwood-agent.service
- [~] Confirm GPU drivers auto-loaded on boot for n2 (currently warning).
- [ ] KMS key-wrap policy change (customer IT action) — BLOCKER for full private key import
- [ ] Final smoke test with a 512-token generation against model 'redwood-small-2' — schedule during daytime window

Notes and commands run (copyable)
- Serial console shortcuts: CTRL+T then ~ for console on new appliance serial.
- Check service: ssh admin@192.168.210.14 && sudo systemctl status redwood-agent.service
- Kernel & GPU check: uname -r -> 6.1.11-custom; nvidia-smi -> shows GPUs but n2 reports ECC warning (see output saved to /tmp/gpu-n2-ecc.txt).
- Network test (from admin host): ip route show; ping -c3 8.8.8.8; curl -v --resolve api.redwood.local:443:10.20.30.5 https://api.redwood.local/health

Environment quirks / gotchas (customer-specific)
- Overlapping subnets: customer has 10.1.0.0/16 used in their internal services. We must use 172.28.x.x management blocks while on site. Never push our default 10.x ranges in customer config.
- Firewall: Outbound to our hosted telemetry endpoints requires HTTP(S) proxy; they restrict direct egress to internet. I left a temporary proxy rule permitting api.redwood.local for the duration of bootstrap. Need IT to make permanent exception if they want telemetry forwarding.
- Rack labeling: The leftmost PDU labeled as "PDU-RED-1" actually feeds circuit C by the room panel. Photos + sticker update done. Tell field ops to cross-check panel labels next visit.
- KVM console: Customer's KVM has timeout ~5min of inactivity and forces serial disconnect; when troubleshooting serial, keep an active session.

Blockers (explicit)
- KMS/HSM policy: Current HSM policy disallows external key import. Customer security has to add a key-wrap exception for our import process (ticket created). Without it, appliance can only use ephemeral keys -> no sealed private deployments. Priority: P1 for production go-live.
- Firmware on node n2: NV-RAM checksum mismatch blocks driver preload; require vendor BIOS push (ETA by vendor: 2026-03-12). Workaround: run with 2x nodes in degraded capacity.

Handoff notes for daytime engineer / next steps
- Helena: please pick up the KMS conversation with customer IT at 09:00 local tomorrow. Ticket JIRA-PRIV-1245 has the request template.
- Ethan: schedule the BIOS flash window with vendor support; prefer early morning maintenance window (02:00-03:00 local).
- Runbook steps for next smoke test (copy to checklist):
  1) Confirm vendor BIOS update applied to n2 and reboot.
  2) From admin host, run full selftest: sudo /opt/redwood/bin/selftest --tokens 512 --model redwood-small-2 > /tmp/selftest-$(date +%F).log
  3) Verify telemetry flush: sudo journalctl -u redwood-agent -n 200 | grep telemetry
  4) Validate certificates: openssl s_client -connect 172.28.4.5:443 -CAfile /etc/ssl/customer-root.pem

Quick troubleshooting notes (if you hit problems)
- If agent fails to register during boot: check /var/log/redwood/agent.log for 401 vs 502. 401 -> KMS key not accepted; 502 -> network/proxy problem.
- If GPU drivers fail to load on a node: collect dmesg | grep -i nvidia and copy /var/log/nvidia-installer.log. Booting with nomodeset may hide the issue; avoid using nomodeset for final tests.
- If management VLAN flaps: look for STP reconvergence on leaf switch (logs at 192.168.210.1) and confirm LLDP shows appliance NICs on correct ports.

Unresolved questions (for product/security)
- Do we have a fallback that allows sealed deployments if customer refuses key-wrap? (short answer: tokenized ephemeral keys only; get product sign-off for acceptable risk)
- Should we add a per-customer default to avoid 10/8 ranges in kickstart files? I think yes; patching appliance build to detect overlap at first-boot would save time.

Photos / artifacts uploaded
- acme-rackA-power-20260309.jpg (rack + PDU labels)
- acme-n2-ecc-snapshot-20260309.log (nvidia-smi output saved)
- serial-n2-boot-20260309.txt (console capture)

Times & local notes
- Onsite arrival 20:30, lights locked by facility by 21:00 (facility staff spacing tight).
- Coffee availability: vending outside—card only. Bring cash next time (shout).

Personal quick wins and followups I want to implement in our tooling
- Add a first-boot subnet conflict detector that warns if appliance default network overlaps with existing routes seen on mgmt interface.
- Make the agent error messaging clearer: distinguish KMS-permission vs KMS-unreachable in logs with actionable remediation docs linked.

Final quick log entry (end of night)
- Left site 23:15. Status: nodes up (degraded), KMS still blocking, vendor BIOS pending. Next engineer to take morning KMS call and schedule BIOS window.

Handoff: tag @HelenaPark on JIRA-PRIV-1245 and ping #private-deployments Slack channel with short summary.

-- Priya N.
(quick field scratchpad; clean version will go to confluence after blockers cleared)
